answer: Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator pays 224 bonds yet holds one position, and the ledge report publishes the merged exposure. The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, because the sable funding graph is rebuilt from the anchor history every epoch. Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 224 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
